16:04 UTC, 21 October 2025
Let me walk you through what's happening in your current implementation and why you're getting the infinite loop.
The Current Flow
When $loadViewData() is called from the view() method:
First call: Method runs, creates a promise, adds it to the execution context with resolved=false, reacted=false
Promise completes: Your async handler schedules an action that sets resolved=true and calls formula.update()
Re-render happens: The update() triggers React to re-render the component
Second call during re-render: view() runs again, calls $loadViewData() again
Finds existing action: The method sees the action exists with resolved=true, reacted=false
Schedules another update: It schedules an action to call formula.update() again and set reacted=true
Loop continues: That update triggers another re-render, and we're back at step 4
The Problem
The issue is that you're scheduling an action to mark something as "reacted" instead of just marking it immediately. By the time that scheduled action runs, another render has already started and found the same "resolved but not reacted" state.
Think of it like this: You're essentially saying "I'll deal with this later" but "later" never comes fast enough because each update triggers a synchronous re-render that checks the state again before "later" arrives.
The Solution
When you encounter a "resolved but not reacted" state, you need to mark it as reacted immediately in the current execution, not schedule it for later. The "reacted" flag basically means "I've seen that this async operation completed and I've handled it."
So the logic should be:
If action exists and is resolved but not reacted → mark as reacted NOW and return
If action exists and is already reacted → it's done, just return
If action doesn't exist → this is the first call, proceed normally
The token system you added could help, but only if you actually use it to prevent duplicate updates. Right now you're passing the token but not checking if it has changed before calling the update.

Looking at your logs, the async methods are completing and scheduling the update actions, but those scheduled actions aren't being executed. The problem is in your schedule method - you're pushing actions to the queue but not running them when the orchestrator is active.
Let's trace what's happening:
Both async methods complete ("async complete" logs twice)
Both schedule an action to context.resolve(id) and formula.update()
These actions get pushed to the orchestrator's action queue
But nothing processes them!
The issue is that scheduled actions are only processed in the useEffect when the orchestrator first becomes active. But your async completions happen AFTER that initial activation, so the actions just sit in the queue.
When you call schedule() and the orchestrator is already active, you should execute the action immediately instead of queuing it:
typescript
private schedule(chemical: $Chemical, action: () => void) {
    const orchestrator = chemical[$orchestrator];
    
    if (orchestrator.active) {
        // Orchestrator is active, run immediately
        action();
    } else {
        // Not active yet, queue for later
        orchestrator.actions.push(action);
    }
}
Your current schedule always pushes to the queue regardless. That's why you see the actions being scheduled but never executing - they're waiting for a useEffect that already ran.
The token approach is good, but it won't help if the updates never fire in the first place. Once you fix the schedule method to actually run actions when the orchestrator is active, your async methods should trigger updates properly.

A few potential solutions:
Don't remove reacted entries immediately - Maybe only clean them up at specific times (like when component unmounts or explicitly reset)
Make token ignore reacted entries - If an entry is marked as reacted, don't include it in the token calculation since it's essentially "done"
Don't remove at all - Just leave reacted entries in place. They'll naturally get cleaned when the component unmounts
Track removal separately - Have a separate "processed" set that doesn't affect the token
The simplest fix is probably option 3 - just don't call remove() in the reacted branch. The entry stays but is marked as fully processed (reacted=true), so it won't trigger any more updates. The clean() method can handle cleanup at appropriate times rather than during render.

Constructor runs once during bond initialization
view() runs on every render
State changes trigger formula.update() which causes re-render
Re-render only calls view(), not the constructor

Call $loadItems() directly from $reload()
Or call $loadItems() from view() when conditions are right
The constructor pattern works for initial load but not for reload because Chemistry's constructors are for one-time initialization during bonding, not reactive to state changes. The reactive part is the view() method.

Yes, there's a gap between render and mount in React (and Chemistry). The lifecycle goes:
Render phase: Component function runs, view() returns JSX
Commit phase: React updates the DOM
Effect phase: useEffect runs (this is when the orchestrator becomes active)
In Chemistry's case, when $reload() is clicked:
It triggers during the already-mounted state (orchestrator is active)
It calls await this.$loadItems() immediately
But there might be a pending $loadItems() from the constructor that hasn't resolved yet
The issue is that your constructor's $loadItems() call might still be running when reload is clicked. Both async operations check items.length > 0 at nearly the same time (both see empty array), so both proceed to add items.
The timing issue is that:
The constructor's $loadItems() starts during bond phase
It's async, so it continues running in the background
When you click reload, it starts ANOTHER $loadItems()
Both are now running concurrently, both adding items to the array
You need a flag that prevents concurrent execution:
typescript
async $loadItems() {
    if (this.loading || this.items.length > 0) return;  // Check loading flag
    this.loading = true;
    // ...rest
}
The loading flag should prevent the second call from proceeding while the first is still running.

class $BondOrchestrator {
    renderQueue = 0;  // Track pending renders

        this.renderQueue++;
        if (this.rendering === 'After') {
            this.rendering = 'Before';
        }
    }

        this.rendering = 'During';
        this.renderQueue = Math.max(0, this.renderQueue - 1);
    }
    
    endRender() {
        this.rendering = this.renderQueue > 0 ? 'Before' : 'After';
    }

Looking at your orchestrator with actions that process in useEffect, here's a sensible approach for handling the different cases:
typescript
const update = (value?: any) => {
    const state = `${orchestrator.mounting}/${orchestrator.rendering}`;
    
    switch(state) {
        case 'Before/Before':  // Not rendered yet
        case 'Before/During':  // First render in progress
            // Queue for useEffect via actions
            orchestrator.actions.push(() => _update(value));
            break;
            
        case 'Before/After':  // Rendered, waiting for mount
            // Queue for useEffect
            orchestrator.actions.push(() => _update(value));
            break;
            
        case 'After/Before':  // Mounted, render already queued
            // Skip - a render is coming anyway
            break;
            
        case 'After/During':  // Mounted, mid-render
            // React will defer this automatically, but we could queue it
            orchestrator.actions.push(() => _update(value));
            break;
            
        case 'After/After':  // Mounted and idle
            // Safe to update immediately
            orchestrator.rendering = 'Before';
            _update(value);
            break;
    }
};
The key principles:
Before mount: Always queue for useEffect since orchestrator isn't active
During render: Queue to avoid React's "setState during render" warning
After mount + After render: Safe to update immediately
Already queued render: Skip redundant updates
For your async completions, you can use the same logic - check the state and decide whether to update immediately or queue the action.
The beauty is that your existing useEffect pattern already processes the action queue, so you're just being smarter about when to queue vs when to execute immediately.

You're right - knowing whether setState will actually trigger a render (by comparing prev and next) lets you predict and update the orchestrator state correctly. Here's the helper function:
typescript
class $Formula {
    private dispatchUpdate(
        setState: (value: any) => void,
        prevState?: any,
        nextState?: any
    ) {
        // Default to fresh objects if not specified
        const prev = prevState ?? {};
        const next = nextState ?? {};
        
        // Check if update will actually trigger render
        const willUpdate = prev !== next;
        
        const orchestrator = this._chemical[$orchestrator];
        const state = `${orchestrator.mounting}Mount/${orchestrator.rendering}Render`;
        
        switch(state) {
            case 'BeforeMount/BeforeRender':
            case 'BeforeMount/DuringRender': 
            case 'BeforeMount/AfterRender':
                // Not mounted yet - queue for useEffect
                orchestrator.actions.push(() => {
                    if (willUpdate) orchestrator.rendering = 'Before';
                    setState(next);
                });
                break;
                
            case 'AfterMount/BeforeRender':
                // Render already queued - skip redundant update
                if (!willUpdate) {
                    setState(next); // Won't trigger render but keeps state consistent
                }
                // If willUpdate, skip - render is coming anyway
                break;
                
            case 'AfterMount/DuringRender':
                // Mid-render - must queue to avoid React error
                orchestrator.actions.push(() => {
                    if (willUpdate) orchestrator.rendering = 'Before';
                    setState(next);
                });
                break;
                
            case 'AfterMount/AfterRender':
                // Idle - safe to update
                if (willUpdate) {
                    orchestrator.rendering = 'Before'; // Transition to render queued
                }
                setState(next);
                break;
        }
    }
    
    // Usage in update methods:
    update(token?: any) {
        this.dispatchUpdate(this._update, this._lastToken, token);
        this._lastToken = token;
    }
}
This gives you:
Predictive orchestrator state updates based on whether render will happen
Proper queuing when not safe to update immediately
Skip redundant updates when render already queued
Clear state names that show mounting and rendering status
The key improvement is using willUpdate to know whether to transition orchestrator.rendering to 'Before', avoiding incorrect state transitions when setState won't actually trigger a render.

    chemical: $Chemical;
    actions: Map<string, Promise<void>> = new Map();
    resolved: Map<string, boolean> = new Map();
    reacted: Map<string, boolean> = new Map();
    unresolved = false;

    constructor(chemical: $Chemical) {
        this.chemical = chemical;
    }

    add(bond: $Bond, action: Promise<void>): string {
        const id = $BondExecutionContext.executionId(this.chemical, bond);
        if (this.actions.has(id)) return id;
        this.actions.set(id, action);
        this.resolved.set(id, false);
        this.reacted.set(id, false);
        this.unresolved = true;
        return id;
    }

    join() {
        const ids: string[] = [];
        const pending: Promise<void>[] = [];
        for (const [id, promise] of this.actions.entries()) {
            if (!this.resolved.get(id)) {
                ids.push(id);
                pending.push(promise);
                this.resolve(id);
            }
        }
        Promise.all(pending).then(() => {
            ids.forEach(id => this.react(id));
        });
    }

    resolve(id: string) {
        this.resolved.set(id, true);
    }

    react(id: string) {
        this.reacted.set(id, true);
    }

    remove(id: string) {
        this.actions.delete(id);
        this.resolved.delete(id);
        this.reacted.delete(id);
    }

    static executionId(chemical: $Chemical, bond: $Bond): string {
        return `${chemical.toString()}[${bond.property}]`;
    }
}

Given that update() and updateState() already use dispatchUpdate, your bondCall implementation can be simpler and focus on:
Idempotency - preventing duplicate calls
State tracking - detecting when updates are needed
Delegating to Formula - letting it handle the lifecycle complexity
Here's an optimal implementation:
typescript
private bondCall(chemical: $Chemical, ...args: any[]): any {
    const context = $Bond.context ?? chemical[$orchestrator].executionContext;
    if (!$Bond.context) $Bond.context = context;

    const id = $BondExecutionContext.executionId(chemical, this);
    const formula = chemical[$formula];
    
    // Check idempotency - if already called, return cached promise
    if (context.actions.has(id)) {
        // Clean up fully processed actions
        if (context.reacted.get(id)) {
            context.remove(id);
        }
        return context.actions.get(id);
    }

    // Bind state and track for dependency detection
    formula.bindState();
    formula.track();
    
    // Execute the method
    let result = this.action!(...args);
    
    // Handle sync methods
    if (!(result instanceof Promise)) {
        formula.check();
        formula.unbindState();
        formula.updateState(); // Uses dispatchUpdate internally
        return result;
    }
    
    // Handle async methods
    const enhancedPromise = result.then(asyncResult => {
        formula.check();
        
        // Check if state changed
        const currentState = formula.state;
        if (this._previousState !== currentState) {
            this._previousState = currentState;
            formula.update(); // Uses dispatchUpdate internally
        }
        
        // Mark as resolved and reacted
        context.resolve(id);
        context.react(id);
        
        return asyncResult;
    });
    
    // Store in context for idempotency
    context.add(this, enhancedPromise);
    this._previousState = formula.state;
    
    return enhancedPromise;
}
Key optimizations:
Let Formula handle dispatch - Both updateState() and update() use dispatchUpdate, so async completions automatically respect lifecycle states
Simple idempotency - Return cached promise if method already called, clean up completed actions
State comparison - Track state before and after to determine if update needed
Clean separation - Sync uses updateState() (with state tracking), async uses update() (simple dispatch)
The BondExecutionContext.join() method can be called strategically (like after render) to batch mark all pending operations as resolved, but individual async completions handle themselves through the formula's dispatch system.
This design leverages your existing dispatch infrastructure while keeping bondCall focused on its core responsibilities: preventing duplicate execution and detecting state changes.

04:57 UTC, 22 October 2025
The queued action gets processed in your useEffect (where you activate the orchestrator and process the actions array).
When the current render completes, React runs useEffect, which processes your action queue. The queued action then calls setState(next), and if willUpdate was true (state actually changed), it sets orchestrator.rendering = 'Before' to mark that a new render is queued, and the setState(next) call triggers React to schedule that render.
So the sequence is:
During render → action queued
Render completes → rendering becomes 'After'
useEffect runs → processes actions
Action executes → calls setState
React schedules new render → rendering becomes 'Before'
New render starts → back to normal flow
The key is that your useEffect is the bridge that safely executes the queued setState after the current render is complete, avoiding React's "cannot update during render" error.

State comparison issue - The _previousStateAsync might not be properly initialized on first run, or the state serialization might not detect array mutations correctly
Update triggers re-render - Component re-renders
Something resets state - Either the component is remounting, or state is being reset
Constructor runs again - Because cleared is false again, it calls $loadItems() again
The key issue is likely in one of these areas:
Array mutation detection: When you push() to an array, the reference stays the same. The state serialization might not detect this as a change, or might detect it incorrectly.
Async state initialization: For constructor-called async methods, _previousStateAsync might not be initialized, causing comparison issues.
Component remounting: If something is causing the component to unmount/remount repeatedly (like a key change or parent re-render), the constructor would run each time.
bondSet recursion: The bondSet calling bondGet() could create a feedback loop if the get triggers tracking that leads to another set.
To debug this, check:
Is $Bond.context available during constructor?
What's the value of _previousStateAsync when the async completes?
Is the component's key stable or changing?
Are the orchestrator lifecycle states correct when the async completes?
The infinite loop suggests the state update from the async completion is somehow triggering a reset that makes the constructor condition if (!this.cleared) true again.

Pause OneDrive

Looking at the bond orchestrator flow, the parent-child binding happens in a specific order:
Parent's bond() method runs - processes props and children
Children are processed - creates child chemicals
Parent's constructor runs - with children as arguments
Child components render - their bond() and constructors run
If the catalogue constructor is running before books have their chapters, the issue is likely that books are being created but not fully bonded when the catalogue constructor executes.
The problem might be in the processElement method of the orchestrator. When it encounters a Chemistry component, it:
Creates the chemical
Adds it to parent's context
But doesn't run the child's bond() yet
So when the parent's constructor runs with these children as arguments, the children exist but haven't been through their own bonding process yet (where they would get THEIR children).
This creates a situation where:
Catalogue gets Book instances
But Books haven't received their Chapter children yet
So book.chapters would be undefined/empty
The orchestrator seems to be doing depth-first creation but breadth-first bonding. You get all the immediate children created, then the parent bonds, THEN the children bond.
To fix this, you might need to either:
Have children fully bond before being passed to parent constructor
Or delay accessing children's children until after mounting
Or use a different pattern where the parent doesn't expect fully-formed children in its constructor

To attach a debugger in VS Code to a TypeScript Next.js app:
Method 1: Built-in VS Code Debugging
Create .vscode/launch.json in your project root:
json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Next.js: debug server-side",
      "type": "node-terminal",
      "request": "launch",
      "command": "npm run dev"
    },
    {
      "name": "Next.js: debug client-side",
      "type": "chrome",
      "request": "launch",
      "url": "http://localhost:3000",
      "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}"
    },
    {
      "name": "Next.js: debug full stack",
      "type": "node-terminal",
      "request": "launch",
      "command": "npm run dev",
      "serverReadyAction": {
        "pattern": "- Local:.+(https?://.+)",
        "uriFormat": "%s",
        "action": "debugWithChrome"
      }
    }
  ]
}
Update your package.json dev script:
json

Press F5 or go to Run → Start Debugging in VS Code

Start your app with debugging enabled:

NODE_OPTIONS='--inspect' npm run dev

Set breakpoints in your TypeScript files in VS Code

Looking at your logs, you're absolutely right - there's a massive inefficiency. Every render is creating NEW chemical instances (Book[867], Chapter[868], etc.) instead of reusing bound components. The CID numbers incrementing to 867+ shows hundreds of unnecessary instances being created.
The core problem is in processElement:
typescript
if (!component.$bound) {
    component = component.$bind(this._chemical);
}
Each render, React passes new function references for your components. So even though you check component.$bound, it's checking a DIFFERENT function object each time - one that doesn't have $bound set. This causes:
$bind gets called again → creates NEW chemical instance
New chemical gets new CID (867, 868, 869...)
Child bonding cascades → all children recreated
Exponential explosion of instances
The fix would be to cache bound components by their function identity, not rely on mutating the function object:
typescript
// Somewhere stable (maybe a WeakMap)
const boundComponents = new WeakMap<Function, $$Component>();

// In processElement
let component: $$Component = boundComponents.get(type) || type;
if (!component.$bound) {
    component = $wrap(func).$Component.$bind(this._chemical);
    boundComponents.set(type, component);
}
This way, the second render would find the already-bound component and reuse it, preventing the cascade of new instances.
The current behavior explains:
Why Chrome was hanging (creating hundreds of components)
Why the logs show thousands of hidden entries
Why Books aren't getting Chapters (different instances each time)
You need a stable way to associate React component functions with their bound Chemistry instances across renders.

The issue is that you ARE rewriting the tree with bound components, but React doesn't use that rewritten tree for the next render.
Here's what's happening:
First render: React gives you <Book> elements with fresh function references
You bind them: Create Book[865], rewrite tree with bound components
React renders your rewritten tree
Second render: React starts over with the ORIGINAL JSX <Book> elements again - these have fresh, unbound function references
Your code sees unbound components and creates new instances
The problem is React always starts from the original JSX on each render:
jsx
// This JSX is evaluated fresh each render
<Catalogue>
    <Book title="...">  {/* New function reference each time */}
        <Chapter />
    </Book>
</Catalogue>
Even though you rewrote the tree with bound components, React doesn't "remember" that. It re-evaluates the JSX, creating new React elements with fresh function references to the original, unbound component functions.
To fix this, you need to:
Cache the binding relationship between the original function and its bound version
When you see the same original function again, return the cached bound version
React's reconciliation works with element types, but you're getting new function references each render. You need a stable mapping from "original Book function" → "bound Book component" that persists across renders, not one that relies on mutating the function object itself.

private _componentCache = new Map<Function, $$Component>();

private processElement(element: React.ReactElement<any>, context: $BondOrchestrationContext) {

    else if (typeof type === 'function') {

Looking at your bond() method, there are multiple places triggering potential re-renders:
bindProps() calls chemical[$formula].refresh()
End of bond() calls chemical[$formula].refresh() again
Each child bonding might trigger its own updates
The issue is that during the INITIAL render/mount, as you process the tree:
Catalogue bonds → refreshes formula
Catalogue processes Book1 → Book1 bonds → refreshes formula → might trigger Catalogue re-render
Book1 processes Chapter1 → Chapter1 bonds → refreshes formula → might cascade up
And so on...
If each bonding triggers a formula refresh that causes a re-render, and re-renders restart the whole bonding process, you get exponential explosion.
The key problem: You're calling ␀0␀ during the bonding phase itself, which might trigger re-renders WHILE you're still building the initial tree.
Consider deferring formula updates until after the entire tree is bonded:
typescript
bond(props: any, parentContext?: $BondOrchestrationContext): any {
    $Bond.reactive = false;  // You already do this
    
    // ... all your bonding logic ...
    
    // Don't call refresh here - defer it
    // chemical[$formula].refresh();
    
    return props;
}
Then batch refresh after the entire tree is processed. The tree rewriting should happen in one pass without triggering intermediate re-renders.
The excessive re-renders aren't from React - they're from your own formula.refresh() calls triggering state updates during the tree construction phase.

But for Chemistry's philosophy of hiding React complexity, you could make it even more seamless by having the framework automatically inject these triggers. When processing the tree in augmentView():
typescript
private augmentView(view: ReactNode): ReactNode {
    const chemical = this._chemical;
    const asyncTriggers = [];
    
    // Detect async methods that should auto-run
    for (const bond of chemical[$formula].bonds.values()) {
        if (bond.isMethod && bond.property.startsWith('$$')) {  // $$ for auto-run
            asyncTriggers.push(
                React.createElement(AsyncTrigger, {
                    key: bond.property,
                    method: bond.action,
                    instance: chemical
                })
            );
        }
    }
    
    // Prepend invisible triggers to the view
    return React.createElement(
        React.Fragment,
        { key: `chem-${chemical[$cid]}` },
        ...asyncTriggers,
        view
    );
}
This way, methods marked with $$ would automatically run when the component renders, without the developer having to write any trigger code. The async execution would be part of the render tree itself, making it predictable and tied to React's lifecycle.

$Do is for guaranteed execution with render-time binding

The mental move you made was finding the general case that encompasses both behaviors. Instead of seeing Do and If as different things, you recognized that "always execute" is just "conditionally execute where condition is always true."
This requires:
Abstracting up a level - Not thinking "Do has no condition, If has a condition" but asking "what if both have conditions, just with different defaults?"
Willingness to add seeming redundancy - Adding _condition = true to Do looks wasteful until you see it enables the inheritance
Seeing constants as variables - Recognizing that a hardcoded true is still a value that can be overridden
Working backwards from the desired API - You knew If needed $condition as a prop, so you found the minimal path to add just that
The general lesson is: When two things are similar, look for the parameterization that makes them identical. Don't create different code paths for different cases - find the general form where the cases are just different parameter values.
To train this thinking:
When you have if/else branches, ask if they could be the same code with different values
When subclassing, try to change only data, not logic
Look for the "degenerate case" - where a general solution with specific parameters reduces to the simple case
The hard part isn't the programming - it's seeing that "unconditional" is just a flavor of "conditional." That's the creative leap that turns 100 lines into 10.

You're absolutely right - async functions returning JSX isn't valid React. React components must be synchronous. An async function returns a Promise<JSX.Element>, not a JSX.Element.
The test is misleading. While $Do handles the Promise correctly (waiting for it to resolve before rendering), the pattern suggests async methods can return JSX directly, which they can't in normal React.
The correct pattern would be:
typescript
async $fetchData() {
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    // Return data, not JSX
    return { message: "Data loaded", value: Math.random() };
}

$renderData() {
    // Synchronous method returns JSX
    if (!this.data) return null;
    return (
        <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#fce4ec' }}>
            {this.data.message}
        </div>
    );
}
Or the async method should update state and let the view render based on that state:
typescript
async $loadData() {
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
    this.data = "Loaded!";  // Update state
    // Don't return JSX
}
The $Do component makes it SEEM like async methods can return JSX because it handles the Promise, but this creates a false mental model. In real React, you can't have async render methods. The tests should demonstrate patterns that reinforce correct React understanding, not obscure it.

        return undefined;  // Actions return undefined by default
    }

    protected _condition = false;
    get $condition() { return this._condition; }
    set $condition(value: boolean) { this._condition = value; }

// In $Chemical class, add tracking for $$ methods:

export class $Chemical {
    private $$executed = new Set<string>();
    
    // In the proxy handler or wherever methods are invoked:
    private invokeMethod(methodName: string, ...args: any[]) {
        // Check for $$ prefix - run exactly once methods
        if (methodName.startsWith('$$')) {
            if (this.$$executed.has(methodName)) {
                return; // Already ran once, skip
            }
            this.$$executed.add(methodName);
        }
        
        // Continue with normal method invocation...
        return this[methodName](...args);
    }
}

// Usage example:
export class $DataComponent extends $Chemical {
    data: any = null;
    
    // Runs exactly once, even if called from multiple places
    async $$loadInitialData() {
        const response = await fetch('/api/data');
        this.data = await response.json();
    }
    
    $DataComponent() {
        this.$$loadInitialData(); // First call - executes
    }
    
    view() {
        this.$$loadInitialData(); // Subsequent calls - skipped
        
        if (!this.data) return <div>Loading...</div>;
        return <div>{this.data.message}</div>;
    }
}

Simplified Async State Management v1
typescript
class $BondExecutionContext {
    chemical: $Chemical;
    actions: Map<string, Promise<void>> = new Map();
    resolved: Map<string, boolean> = new Map();
    reacted: Map<string, boolean> = new Map();

    // Generate a unique state fingerprint for the current async context
    getState(): string {
        const keys = Array.from(this.actions.keys());
        const resolved = Array.from(this.resolved.values());
        const reacted = Array.from(this.reacted.values());
        
        return $Represent.symbolize([keys, resolved, reacted], 'fast');
    }
    
    // ... rest of the class
}

// Then in bondCall, use state comparison to prevent re-execution
private bondCall(chemical: $Chemical, ...args: any[]): any {
    let id: string | undefined;
    const context = $Bond.context;
    const formula = chemical[$formula];
    
    if (context) {
        id = $BondExecutionContext.executionId(chemical, this);
        
        // If this method has already been called, skip it
        if (context.actions.has(id)) {
            return; // Already called, idempotent
        }
    }
    
    formula.bindState();
    formula.track();
    let result = this.action!(...args);
    
    const isAsync = result instanceof Promise;
    if (!isAsync) {
        formula.check();
        formula.updateState();
    }
    
    formula.unbind();
    if (!isAsync) return result;
    
    if (!context) {
        result.then(() => {
            formula.update();
        });
        return;
    }
    
    // Add the async action with its state
    const initialState = context.getState();
    
    context.add(this, result.then(() => {
        // Only update if state has actually changed
        const newState = context.getState();
        if (initialState !== newState) {
            formula.update();
        }
    }));
}

// Or even simpler - just track if method was called this render
class $BondExecutionContext {
    chemical: $Chemical;
    called: Set<string> = new Set();  // Methods called this render
    pending: Map<string, Promise<void>> = new Map();  // Active promises
    
    reset() {
        this.called.clear();  // Clear for next render
    }
    
    markCalled(bond: $Bond): boolean {
        const id = $BondExecutionContext.executionId(this.chemical, bond);
        if (this.called.has(id)) {
            return false;  // Already called
        }
        this.called.add(id);
        return true;  // First call
    }
}

        if (!context.markCalled(this)) {
            return;
        }

        formula.check();
        formula.updateState();
    }
    
    formula.unbind();
    if (!isAsync) return result;

    result.then(() => {
        formula.update();
    });

Simplified BondOrchestrationContext without Prototypal Logic v1
typescript
class $BondOrchestrationContext {
    private parameters: $BondParameter[];
    private parameterIndex = -1;
    arguments: $BondArguments;
    args: any[] = [];
    chemical: $Chemical;
    node: any = undefined;
    children: ReactNode[] = [];
    childContexts: $BondOrchestrationContext[] = [];
    singleton: boolean = false;
    parameter?: $BondParameter;
    argsValid?: boolean = true;
    parent?: $BondOrchestrationContext;
    
    private _isModified = false;

    get isElement() { 
        return React.isValidElement(this.node);
    }

    get isModified() { 
        return this._isModified; 
    }
    
    set isModified(value: boolean) { 
        this._isModified = value;
        if (value && this.parent) {
            this.parent.isModified = value;  // Fixed: was missing the assignment
        }
    }

    constructor(chemical: $Chemical, parameters: $BondParameter[] = []) {
        this.chemical = chemical;
        this.parameters = parameters;
        this.arguments = new $BondArguments(parameters || []);
        this.args = this.arguments.values;
    }

    next(node: any): $BondOrchestrationContext {
        // Create a new instance instead of cloning prototypally
        const context = new $BondOrchestrationContext(this.chemical, this.parameters);
        
        // Copy relevant properties
        context.parameterIndex = this.parameterIndex;
        context.arguments = this.arguments;  // Share the same arguments instance
        context.args = this.args;  // Share the same args array reference
        context.singleton = this.singleton;
        context.parameter = this.parameter;
        context.argsValid = this.argsValid;
        context.parent = this.parent;
        context.children = this.children;  // Share the same children array
        context.childContexts = this.childContexts;  // Share the same childContexts array
        
        // Set the new node
        context.node = node;
        
        // Update parameter tracking
        if (!context.parameter && context.parameterIndex === -1) {
            if (context.parameters && context.parameters.length > 0) {
                context.parameterIndex = 0;
                context.parameter = context.parameters[context.parameterIndex];
            } else {
                context.argsValid = false;
            }
        } else if (context.parameter && context.parameter.isSpread) {
            // Spread parameter continues consuming all remaining args
            context.args = context.arguments.values;
        } else if (context.parameter && !context.parameter.isSpread) {
            // Move to next parameter
            context.parameterIndex++;
            if (context.parameters && context.parameterIndex < context.parameters.length) {
                context.parameter = context.parameters[context.parameterIndex];
                if (context.parameter && context.parameter.isSpread) {
                    context.args = context.arguments.values;
                }
            } else {
                context.parameter = undefined;
                context.argsValid = false;
            }
        }
        
        return context;
    }

    array(): $BondOrchestrationContext {
        // Create a fresh context for array processing
        const context = new $BondOrchestrationContext(this.chemical, []);
        
        // Set up array-specific properties
        context.parent = this;
        context.args = [];
        context.parameters = [];
        context.parameterIndex = -1;
        context.parameter = { isArray: true, isSpread: false };
        context.children = [];
        
        // Add the new arrays to parent's args and children
        this.args.push(context.args);
        this.children.push(context.children);
        
        return context;
    }

    child(chemical: $Chemical, props: any): any {
        console.log('context.child called:', chemical.toString(), 'props.children:', props.children);
        
        if (chemical[$lastProps] === props) {
            console.log('Props unchanged, returning cached');
            return props;
        }
        
        console.log('Bonding child chemical');
        props = chemical[$orchestrator].bond(props, this);
        chemical[$lastProps] = props;
        
        console.log('Child bonded, returning props');
        return props;
    }

    build(): any {
        if (!this.isModified) {
            return undefined;
        }
        
        return this.singleton && this.children.length === 1 
            ? this.children[0] 
            : this.children;
    }
}

// Test 4: Void/undefined returning actions
export class $VoidActions extends $Chemical {
    sideEffectCount = 0;
    doEffectCount = 0;
    runSideEffect = false;
    
    $ifSideEffect() {
        this.sideEffectCount++;
        // Returns undefined - side effect only

    $doSideEffect() {
        this.doEffectCount++;
        // Returns undefined - side effect only
    }
    
    $toggleCondition() {
        this.runSideEffect = !this.runSideEffect;
    }
    
    $triggerNewDoAction() {
        // Force a new function reference
        this.$doSideEffect = () => {
            this.doEffectCount++;
        };
    }
    
    view() {

                <div style={{ marginBottom: '15px' }}>
                    <div>If side effects run: <strong>{this.sideEffectCount}</strong> times</div>

                    <button onClick={this.$toggleCondition}>
                        Toggle Condition ({this.runSideEffect ? 'ON' : 'OFF'})
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div>Do side effects run: <strong>{this.doEffectCount}</strong> times</div>
                    <Do result={this.$doSideEffect} />
                    <button onClick={this.$triggerNewDoAction}>
                        Change Do Action
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Actions execute even if returning undefined<br/>
                    ✓ Nothing renders (Undefined component)<br/>
                    ✓ Side effects are observable
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

                            if (this.correctMethod) {
                                return <Do result={this.$validMethod} />;
                            } else {
                                return <Do result={invalidAction} />;
                            }
                        } catch (e: any) {
                            this.errorMessage = e.message;
                            return (
                                <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#d32f2f' }}>
                                    ⚠️ Error caught: {e.message}
                                </div>
                            );
                        }
                    })()}
                    
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleMethod} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                        Toggle to {this.correctMethod ? 'Arrow Function' : 'Method Reference'}
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                        Testing $If with arrow function:
                    </div>
                    
                    {(() => {
                        try {
                            return <If condition={this.showError} result={() => this.$validMethod()} />;
                        } catch (e: any) {
                            return (
                                <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#d32f2f' }}>
                                    ⚠️ Error caught: {e.message}
                                </div>
                            );
                        }
                    })()}
                    
                    <button onClick={this.$showCondition} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                        Trigger If Condition
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Throws error for arrow functions<br/>
                    ✓ Works correctly with method references<br/>
                    ✓ Error message guides to correct usage
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 5: Void/undefined returning actions
export class $VoidActions extends $Chemical {
    sideEffectCount = 0;
    doEffectCount = 0;
    runSideEffect = false;
    
    $ifSideEffect() {
        this.sideEffectCount++;
        // Returns undefined - side effect only
    }
    
    $doSideEffect() {
        this.doEffectCount++;
        // Returns undefined - side effect only
    }
    
    $toggleCondition() {
        this.runSideEffect = !this.runSideEffect;
    }
    
    $reset() {
        this.sideEffectCount = 0;
        this.doEffectCount = 0;
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #607d8b', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 5: Void/Undefined Returning Actions</h4>
                
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '15px' }}>
                    <div>If side effects run: <strong>{this.sideEffectCount}</strong> times</div>
                    <If condition={this.runSideEffect} result={this.$ifSideEffect} />
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleCondition}>
                        Toggle Condition ({this.runSideEffect ? 'ON' : 'OFF'})

                <div>
                    <div>Do side effects run: <strong>{this.doEffectCount}</strong> times</div>

// Create component instances
const IfBasic = new $IfBasic().Component;
const DoBasic = new $DoBasic().Component;
const AsyncActions = new $AsyncActions().Component;
const VoidActions = new $VoidActions().Component;
const WeirdReturns = new $WeirdReturns().Component;
const ChemicalReturns = new $ChemicalReturns().Component;

export default function IfDoTests() {
    return (
        <div style={{ padding: '40px', maxWidth: '1200px', margin: '0 auto' }}>
            <h1>$If and $Do Component Tests</h1>
            <p style={{ color: '#666', marginBottom: '30px' }}>
                Testing Chemistry's conditional execution components: $If executes based on condition, $Do always executes
            </p>
            
            <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: '20px' }}>
                <IfBasic />
                <DoBasic />
                <AsyncActions />
                <VoidActions />
                <WeirdReturns />
                <ChemicalReturns />
            </div>
            
            <div style={{ 
                marginTop: '40px', 
                padding: '20px', 
                background: '#f0f8ff', 
                borderRadius: '8px',
                border: '1px solid #2196f3'
            }}>
                <h3>📝 Key Behaviors</h3>
                <ul style={{ margin: '10px 0', paddingLeft: '20px' }}>
                    <li><strong>$If</strong>: Only executes when condition is true, re-executes when action changes while true</li>
                    <li><strong>$Do</strong>: Always executes, re-executes whenever action reference changes</li>
                    <li>Both handle async actions by showing nothing while loading (Undefined component)</li>
                    <li>Both can return JSX, Chemicals, or undefined (for side effects)</li>
                    <li>Non-React return types (strings, numbers) render as text nodes</li>
                    <li>Chemical returns are automatically converted to their Components</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
        </div>
    );
}

// Test 1: $If with condition toggle and sync TSX result
export class $IfBasic extends $Chemical {

    }
}

// Test 3: Async actions for both $If and $Do
export class $AsyncActions extends $Chemical {
    loadIf = false;
    doVersion = 1;
    
    async $asyncIfAction() {
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e3f2fd', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                📦 If: Async loaded after 1.5s! Time: {new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    async $asyncDoAction() {
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#fce4ec', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                🚀 Do: Async v{this.doVersion} loaded after 1s!
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    $toggleIf() {
        this.loadIf = !this.loadIf;
    }
    
    $changeDoVersion() {
        this.doVersion++;
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #ff9800', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 3: Async Actions (Loading States)</h4>
                
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '15px' }}>
                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold', marginBottom: '5px' }}>If Component (conditional async):</div>
                    <If condition={this.loadIf} result={this.$asyncIfAction} />
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleIf} style={{ marginTop: '5px' }}>
                        {this.loadIf ? 'Hide' : 'Load'} Async Content
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold', marginBottom: '5px' }}>Do Component (always async):</div>
                    <Do result={this.$asyncDoAction} />
                    <button onClick={this.$changeDoVersion} style={{ marginTop: '5px' }}>
                        Reload (v{this.doVersion + 1})
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Shows nothing while loading<br/>
                    ✓ Shows result after promise resolves<br/>
                    ✓ Re-triggers on action change
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

const IfBasic = new $IfBasic().Component;
const DoBasic = new $DoBasic().Component;
const AsyncActions = new $AsyncActions().Component;
const ArrowFunctionError = new $ArrowFunctionError().Component;
const VoidActions = new $VoidActions().Component;
const WeirdReturns = new $WeirdReturns().Component;
const ChemicalReturns = new $ChemicalReturns().Component;

export default function IfDoTests() {
    return (
        <div style={{ padding: '40px', maxWidth: '1200px', margin: '0 auto' }}>
            <h1>$If and $Do Component Tests</h1>
            <p style={{ color: '#666', marginBottom: '30px' }}>
                Testing Chemistry's conditional execution components: $If executes based on condition, $Do always executes
            </p>
            
            <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: '20px' }}>
                <IfBasic />
                <DoBasic />
                <AsyncActions />
                <VoidActions />
                <WeirdReturns />
                <ChemicalReturns />
            </div>
            
            <div style={{ 
                marginTop: '40px', 
                padding: '20px', 
                background: '#f0f8ff', 
                borderRadius: '8px',
                border: '1px solid #2196f3'
            }}>
                <h3>📝 Key Behaviors</h3>
                <ul style={{ margin: '10px 0', paddingLeft: '20px' }}>
                    <li><strong>$If</strong>: Only executes when condition is true, re-executes when action changes while true</li>
                    <li><strong>$Do</strong>: Always executes, re-executes whenever action reference changes</li>
                    <li>Both handle async actions by showing nothing while loading (Undefined component)</li>
                    <li>Both can return JSX, Chemicals, or undefined (for side effects)</li>
                    <li>Non-React return types (strings, numbers) render as text nodes</li>
                    <li>Chemical returns are automatically converted to their Components</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
        </div>
    );
}

'use client'
import { $Chemical, If, Do } from '@/chemistry';
import React from 'react';

// Test 1: $If with condition toggle and sync TSX result
export class $IfBasic extends $Chemical {
    showMessage = false;
    messageVersion = 1;
    
    $toggleCondition() {
        this.showMessage = !this.showMessage;
    }
    
    $changeMessage() {
        this.messageVersion++;
    }
    
    $getMessage() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e8f5e9', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                ✅ Message v{this.messageVersion} is showing!
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #4caf50', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 1: $If - Basic Condition & TSX Result</h4>
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                    Condition: <strong>{this.showMessage ? 'TRUE' : 'FALSE'}</strong>
                </div>
                <If condition={this.showMessage} result={this.$getMessage} />
                <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '10px', marginTop: '10px' }}>
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleCondition}>Toggle Condition</button>
                    <button onClick={this.$changeMessage}>Change Message</button>
                </div>
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Shows message when condition true<br/>
                    ✓ Hides when condition false<br/>
                    ✓ Updates message when action changes
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 2: $Do with changing actions
export class $DoBasic extends $Chemical {
    actionType: 'greeting' | 'time' | 'random' = 'greeting';
    
    $showGreeting() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#f3e5f5', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                👋 Hello from Do component!
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    $showTime() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#fff3e0', borderRadius: '4px' }}>

            </div>
        );
    }
    
    $showRandom() {
        return (

                🎲 Random number: {Math.floor(Math.random() * 100)}
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    getCurrentAction() {
        switch(this.actionType) {
            case 'greeting': return this.$showGreeting;
            case 'time': return this.$showTime;
            case 'random': return this.$showRandom;
        }
    }
    
    view() {
        return (

// Test 3: Async actions for both $If and $Do
export class $AsyncActions extends $Chemical {
    loadIf = false;
    doVersion = 1;
    
    async $asyncIfAction() {
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e3f2fd', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                📦 If: Async loaded after 1.5s! Time: {new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    async $asyncDoAction() {
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#fce4ec', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                🚀 Do: Async v{this.doVersion} loaded after 1s!
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    $toggleIf() {
        this.loadIf = !this.loadIf;
    }
    
    $changeDoVersion() {
        this.doVersion++;
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #ff9800', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 3: Async Actions (Loading States)</h4>
                
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '15px' }}>
                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold', marginBottom: '5px' }}>If Component (conditional async):</div>
                    <If condition={this.loadIf} result={this.$asyncIfAction} />
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleIf} style={{ marginTop: '5px' }}>
                        {this.loadIf ? 'Hide' : 'Load'} Async Content
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold', marginBottom: '5px' }}>Do Component (always async):</div>
                    <Do result={this.$asyncDoAction} />
                    <button onClick={this.$changeDoVersion} style={{ marginTop: '5px' }}>
                        Reload (v{this.doVersion + 1})
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Shows nothing while loading<br/>
                    ✓ Shows result after promise resolves<br/>
                    ✓ Re-triggers on action change
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 4: Arrow Function Error Detection
export class $ArrowFunctionError extends $Chemical {
    errorMessage = '';
    showError = false;
    correctMethod = true;
    
    $validMethod() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e8f5e9', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                ✅ Valid method reference passed
            </div>
        );
    }
    
    $toggleMethod() {
        this.correctMethod = !this.correctMethod;
        this.errorMessage = '';
    }
    
    $showCondition() {
        this.showError = true;
    }
    
    $hideCondition() {
        this.showError = false;
    }
    
    view() {
        // Intentionally create an arrow function to test error
        const invalidAction = () => this.$validMethod();
        
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #f44336', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 4: Arrow Function Error Detection</h4>
                
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '15px' }}>
                    <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                        Testing: <strong>{this.correctMethod ? 'Valid Method Reference' : 'Arrow Function (Should Error)'}</strong>
                    </div>
                    
                    {(() => {
                        try {
                            if (this.correctMethod) {
                                return <Do result={this.$validMethod} />;
                            } else {
                                return <Do result={invalidAction} />;
                            }
                        } catch (e: any) {
                            this.errorMessage = e.message;
                            return (
                                <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#d32f2f' }}>
                                    ⚠️ Error caught: {e.message}
                                </div>
                            );
                        }
                    })()}
                    
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleMethod} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                        Toggle to {this.correctMethod ? 'Arrow Function' : 'Method Reference'}
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                        Testing $If with arrow function:
                    </div>
                    
                    {(() => {
                        try {
                            return <If condition={this.showError} result={() => this.$validMethod()} />;
                        } catch (e: any) {
                            return (
                                <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#d32f2f' }}>
                                    ⚠️ Error caught: {e.message}
                                </div>
                            );
                        }
                    })()}
                    
                    <button onClick={this.$showCondition} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                        Trigger If Condition
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Throws error for arrow functions<br/>
                    ✓ Works correctly with method references<br/>
                    ✓ Error message guides to correct usage
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 5: Void/undefined returning actions
export class $VoidActions extends $Chemical {
    sideEffectCount = 0;
    doEffectCount = 0;
    runSideEffect = false;
    
    $ifSideEffect() {
        this.sideEffectCount++;
        // Returns undefined - side effect only
    }
    
    $doSideEffect() {
        this.doEffectCount++;
        // Returns undefined - side effect only
    }
    
    $toggleCondition() {
        this.runSideEffect = !this.runSideEffect;
    }
    
    $reset() {
        this.sideEffectCount = 0;
        this.doEffectCount = 0;
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #607d8b', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 5: Void/Undefined Returning Actions</h4>
                
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '15px' }}>
                    <div>If side effects run: <strong>{this.sideEffectCount}</strong> times</div>
                    <If condition={this.runSideEffect} result={this.$ifSideEffect} />
                    <button onClick={this.$toggleCondition}>
                        Toggle Condition ({this.runSideEffect ? 'ON' : 'OFF'})
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div>Do side effects run: <strong>{this.doEffectCount}</strong> times</div>
                    <Do result={this.$doSideEffect} />
                    <button onClick={this.$reset} style={{ marginLeft: '10px' }}>
                        Reset Counts
                    </button>
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Actions execute even if returning undefined<br/>
                    ✓ Nothing renders (Undefined component)<br/>
                    ✓ Side effects are observable
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

'use client'
import { $Chemical, When, If } from '@/chemistry';

// Test 1: Basic When with async data loading
export class $WhenDataLoader extends $Chemical {
    userData: any = null;
    loadCount = 0;
    
    async $loadUserData() {
        this.loadCount++;
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
        this.userData = {
            name: 'John Doe',
            email: 'john@example.com',
            loadedAt: new Date().toLocaleTimeString(),
            loadNumber: this.loadCount
        };
    }
    
    $reset() {
        this.userData = null;
        this.loadCount = 0;
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #4caf50', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 1: When - Async Data Loading</h4>
                <When action={this.$loadUserData}>
                    <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e8f5e9', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                        <div><strong>User Loaded!</strong></div>
                        <div>Name: {this.userData?.name}</div>
                        <div>Email: {this.userData?.email}</div>
                        <div>Loaded at: {this.userData?.loadedAt}</div>
                        <div style={{ fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                            Load #{this.userData?.loadNumber}
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </When>
                <button onClick={this.$reset} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                    Reset Data
                </button>
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Children render after async completes<br/>
                    ✓ Shows loading (nothing) while pending<br/>
                    ✓ Data is available when children render
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 2: If with conditional async operations
export class $IfConditionalLoader extends $Chemical {
    shouldLoad = false;
    items: string[] = [];
    loadStarted = false;
    
    async $fetchItems() {
        this.loadStarted = true;
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
        this.items = [
            'Item A - ' + Math.floor(Math.random() * 100),
            'Item B - ' + Math.floor(Math.random() * 100),
            'Item C - ' + Math.floor(Math.random() * 100)
        ];
    }
    
    $toggleCondition() {
        this.shouldLoad = !this.shouldLoad;
        if (!this.shouldLoad) {
            this.items = [];
            this.loadStarted = false;
        }
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #2196f3', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 2: If - Conditional Async Loading</h4>
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                    Load condition: <strong>{this.shouldLoad ? 'ON' : 'OFF'}</strong>
                    {this.loadStarted && !this.items.length && ' (Loading...)'}
                </div>
                <If condition={this.shouldLoad} action={this.$fetchItems}>

// Test 5: Error handling in async actions
export class $ErrorHandling extends $Chemical {
    attempts = 0;
    lastError: string | null = null;
    data: any = null;
    
    async $riskyOperation() {
        this.attempts++;
        this.lastError = null;
        
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
        
        // Fail on odd attempts
        if (this.attempts % 2 !== 0) {
            this.lastError = `Operation failed on attempt ${this.attempts}`;
            throw new Error(this.lastError);
        }
        
        this.data = {
            success: true,
            message: `Success on attempt ${this.attempts}`,
            timestamp: new Date().toLocaleTimeString()
        };
    }
    
    $retry() {
        this.data = null;
        // Force re-execution by changing the function reference
        const oldMethod = this.$riskyOperation;
        this.$riskyOperation = async function(this: $ErrorHandling) {
            return oldMethod.call(this);
        }.bind(this);
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #f44336', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 5: Error Handling</h4>
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                    Attempts: {this.attempts} (fails on odd numbers)
                </div>
                <When action={this.$riskyOperation}>
                    <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e8f5e9', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                        {this.data?.message} at {this.data?.timestamp}
                    </div>
                </When>
                {this.lastError && (
                    <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#c62828' }}>
                        Error: {this.lastError}
                    </div>
                )}
                <button onClick={this.$retry} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                    Retry Operation
                </button>
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Errors don't crash the component<br/>
                    ✓ Can retry failed operations<br/>
                    ✓ Children only render on success
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 7: Arrow function detection
export class $ArrowFunctionTest extends $Chemical {
    data = 'Initial';
    errorCaught = false;
    errorMessage = '';
    
    $validMethod() {
        this.data = 'Method executed';
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #795548', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 7: Arrow Function Detection</h4>

                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>Valid method reference:</div>
                    <When action={this.$validMethod}>
                        <div style={{ padding: '8px', background: '#efebe9', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                            ✓ {this.data}
                        </div>
                    </When>
                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>Arrow function (will error):</div>
                    {(() => {
                        try {
                            return <When action={() => this.$validMethod()}>
                                <div>This won't render</div>
                            </When>;
                        } catch (e: any) {
                            return (
                                <div style={{ padding: '8px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#c62828' }}>
                                    ⚠️ {e.message}
                                </div>
                            );
                        }
                    })()}
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Detects and prevents arrow functions<br/>
                    ✓ Clear error message guides to correct usage<br/>
                    ✓ Method references work correctly
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

            }}>
                <h3>📝 Key Patterns</h3>
                <ul style={{ margin: '10px 0', paddingLeft: '20px' }}>
                    <li><strong>$When</strong>: Executes action, renders children when complete</li>
                    <li><strong>$If</strong>: Same as When but only when condition is true</li>
                    <li>Actions do work (load data, compute values) but don't return JSX</li>
                    <li>Children have access to data loaded by the action</li>
                    <li>Shows nothing while async actions are pending</li>

                    <li>Errors in actions don't crash the component</li>
                </ul>
            </div>
        </div>
    );
}

                </div>
                
                <div>
                    <div style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>Arrow function (will error):</div>
                    {(() => {
                        try {
                            return <When action={() => this.$validMethod()}>
                                <div>This won't render</div>
                            </When>;
                        } catch (e: any) {
                            return (
                                <div style={{ padding: '8px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#c62828' }}>
                                    ⚠️ {e.message}
                                </div>
                            );
                        }
                    })()}
                </div>
                
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Detects and prevents arrow functions<br/>
                    ✓ Clear error message guides to correct usage<br/>
                    ✓ Method references work correctly
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

// Test 5: Error handling in async actions
export class $ErrorHandling extends $Chemical {
    attempts = 0;
    lastError: string | null = null;
    data: any = null;
    
    async $riskyOperation() {
        this.attempts++;
        this.lastError = null;
        
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
        
        // Fail on odd attempts
        if (this.attempts % 2 !== 0) {
            this.lastError = `Operation failed on attempt ${this.attempts}`;
            throw new Error(this.lastError);
        }
        
        this.data = {
            success: true,
            message: `Success on attempt ${this.attempts}`,
            timestamp: new Date().toLocaleTimeString()
        };
    }
    
    $retry() {
        this.data = null;
        // Force re-execution by changing the function reference
        const oldMethod = this.$riskyOperation;
        this.$riskyOperation = async function(this: $ErrorHandling) {
            return oldMethod.call(this);
        }.bind(this);
    }
    
    view() {
        return (
            <div style={{ padding: '15px', border: '1px solid #f44336', borderRadius: '8px' }}>
                <h4>Test 5: Error Handling</h4>
                <div style={{ marginBottom: '10px' }}>
                    Attempts: {this.attempts} (fails on odd numbers)
                </div>
                <When action={this.$riskyOperation}>
                    <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#e8f5e9', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
                        {this.data?.message} at {this.data?.timestamp}
                    </div>
                </When>
                {this.lastError && (
                    <div style={{ padding: '10px', background: '#ffebee', borderRadius: '4px', color: '#c62828' }}>
                        Error: {this.lastError}
                    </div>
                )}
                <button onClick={this.$retry} style={{ marginTop: '10px' }}>
                    Retry Operation
                </button>
                <div style={{ marginTop: '10px', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>
                    ✓ Errors don't crash the component<br/>
                    ✓ Can retry failed operations<br/>
                    ✓ Children only render on success
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
}

                    </div>
